After returning to the room-service station, the waiter debits the guest's account.
The waiter may wait to do the billing if he has another order to prepare or deliver.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use bpmn:sequenceFlow for execution order between flow nodes in the same process or subprocess scope; set valid sourceRef and targetRef values.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.

When the description states that approval is followed by required activities and that the process closes after those activities: Connect the approval outcome through all required follow-up activities to the process end, preserving any ordering or parallelism stated in the description.

When the description states that a distinct body of work is started and also describes the work performed within it: Model the stated act of starting the work as a separate activity before the workflow that performs it; do not use that workflow, a subprocess, or a start event as a substitute for the activity.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

result.rule: When the description states that a distinct body of work is started and also describes the work performed within it: Model the stated act of starting the work as a separate activity before the workflow that performs it; do not use that workflow, a subprocess, or a start event as a substitute for the activity.

When the description explicitly states that an actor performs an action that initiates the described process: Model the stated action as an activity in the actor’s scope; do not use a start event representing the resulting occurrence as a substitute for that activity. Represent the process start separately with an appropriate start event.

When the description names an action and then describes work it comprises, without identifying a distinct process scope or an independent trigger for that work: Model the named action as an activity in the current process, and represent the constituent work at the level of detail stated. Do not replace the action with a subprocess and its own start and end events solely because the description lists work it comprises.

When the description states a final activity but does not explicitly identify the outcome that ends the process: Use a generic end-event label rather than inferring a specific business outcome from that activity.
